The module uses rustls/ring and dynamically needs musl libc only. The reference OPENSSL_STATIC setting is unused: no openssl-sys or static OpenSSL is in its frozen closure. Bind writable /var/lib/p11lab owned by the caller, mode 0700; private /run/p11lab mode 0700 and container PID/network namespaces are required. Each independent shard/client owns its volume and container. Fixed loopback ports are 8080/8443 and 2379/2380; no host/shared networking. Both services bind 127.0.0.1, including etcd peer traffic; no TAP privileges or host mounts.

P11LAB_LABEL defaults to P11Lab, 1..32 ASCII letters/digits/spaces/dot/underscore/hyphen. First init requires caller PIN/operator and SO/admin inputs of 10..200 printable ASCII characters. Common file/scalar secret validation precedes state creation. Native C_InitToken and C_InitPIN return 0x54; provision the server and operator explicitly through its HTTPS API.

Unlock passphrase is independently generated at runtime and stored under nethsm/unlock. nethsm/admin and p11nethsm.conf contain the caller admin secret at mode 0600; operator PIN is not retained in the module config. The caller PIN authenticates operator C_Login. The administrator config enables upstream automatic privileged key generation, import/deletion and administration even without a caller SO login: applications able to read this config have administrator authority. This is a disposable development isolation boundary, not a protected multi-user HSM.

Existing init validates static state and native readiness and ignores changed input credential files. Static exact-byte complete/config checks, .init-lock, an exclusive volume lease, private control lock, known etcd roster/Bolt header, ownership/mode/link checks run before any native process. Missing, partial, foreign, incompatible and occupied state is refused. No reset, reprovisioning, PIN change or state-changing retry is implicit.

init/health/exec use a P11Lab C supervisor: direct service children, real Unprovisioned/Operational API gating, bounded startup and 64-KiB log sinks, native token/label checks, required-service death monitoring, signal forwarding, TERM/KILL escalation and subreaper/adopted-child cleanup. Services live for the operation/application lifetime. No permanent server/server-ready operation is needed; the preferred proxy daemon runs through the same exec.

Clean restart unlocks an already provisioned Locked server with its private generated passphrase; it never reprovisions an Unprovisioned server behind a completion marker. Persistent keys and operator/admin credentials survive restart. Reset is explicit caller removal/replacement of disposable state after all operations stop. Native failed authentication can trigger server rate limits; no transparent retry is added. An etcd SIGKILL can retain native WAL 0.tmp; static checks refuse this partial state without deletion or repair. Clean shutdown/restart is supported; crash recovery is unqualified.

general-token is FALSIFIED: the unchanged generated-key consumer returns C_DestroyObject(public cleanup) CK_RV=0x60 after private-key deletion invalidates the public alias. Preserve this failure. Restricted persistent P-256 generation/signing is assessed independently; wider mechanisms, native object/session semantics, concurrent clients, crash/power-loss recovery, hardware security and other architectures/libcs are unqualified. Wrong operator PIN is preserved as native 0x103.
